dimensions.question: What can a prospective Sailor establish about Scarlet Lady, its current offer and the physical/digital structure of the ship before booking?
dimensions.scopeChange: Case #26 applies the standard public-evidence question to a mobile, ship-based hospitality institution. Sufficient applies only to public identity and offer representation, not to operational quality or guest outcomes.

observations.text: Virgin Voyages identifies Scarlet Lady as its first ship and publishes current itinerary options, 3D deck plans, refreshed onboard spaces, dining, entertainment and a photo gallery.
The deck-plan presentation explicitly supports pre-voyage orientation by helping prospective Sailors locate cabins, pool areas, bars and restaurants.

unanswered: Search, comparison and booking usability across desktop and mobile were not tested.
Marketing representation does not establish actual onboard wayfinding performance.
dimensions.reason: Identity and the broad public offer are supported, but booking usability, responsive presentation and operational wayfinding remain untested.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Test live itinerary comparison, booking entry points and responsive presentation separately.

dimensions.question: Which pre-voyage choices can be reserved, when do they unlock, and how do fare or cabin categories affect access?
dimensions.scopeChange: The case emphasizes time-gated access because dining and other experiences unlock at different stages of the journey.

observations.text: Dining reservation access varies by booking date, fare option and accommodation class; for bookings on or after 7 October 2025, published windows range from 15 days for some standard-cabin fares to 120 days for RockStar and Mega RockStar quarters.
Other onboard experiences such as spa, entertainment and tattoos are published as reservable once onboard rather than during the same pre-voyage window.
Shore Things can be booked before sailing through the app, My Account, Sailor Services or a travel partner.

unanswered: Live inventory, booking friction, modification and cancellation flows were not tested.
The practical effect of unequal reservation windows on availability was not measured.
dimensions.reason: Published entitlement and timing rules are clear, but availability and execution are untested.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Inspect live booking flows and record how inventory, modifications, cancellation and waitlist recovery behave.

dimensions.question: What must a Sailor prepare before reaching the terminal, including check-in, accessibility and special-assistance needs?
dimensions.scopeChange: The ship context makes identity, documentation, arrival-slot selection and advance assistance part of the pre-arrival system.

observations.text: Virgin directs Sailors to complete Ready to Sail check-in in the app and select a Terminal Arrival Time before embarkation.
Virgin publishes advance channels for accessibility and medical requests, including accessible cabins, embarkation/disembarkation assistance, dietary needs and other accommodations.
The accessibility FAQ asks Sailors needing certain accommodations to contact the Accessibility Team and, for accessible-cabin needs, to complete the relevant request process in advance.

unanswered: Document-verification failure, incomplete check-in and late assistance-request recovery were not tested.
Individual accommodation acceptance and fulfilment cannot be inferred from published request channels.
dimensions.reason: Preparation requirements and assistance routes are documented, but execution and exception handling remain unverified.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Inspect travel-document requirements, failed-check-in recovery and accommodation-confirmation workflows.

dimensions.question: How are terminal arrival, luggage, check-in, boarding and the transition onto the ship coordinated?
dimensions.scopeChange: Arrival is treated as a timed cross-boundary transition between terminal operations and ship operations.

observations.text: General boarding is published as generally beginning at 2:15 p.m., while Sailors must follow their selected Terminal Arrival Time to complete terminal check-in.
Virgin publishes port-specific luggage handling and notes that early luggage drop does not create earlier terminal access.
The Band becomes a voyage-specific credential for cabin access and touchless payment after embarkation.

unanswered: Queueing, missed arrival slots, document exceptions and real transfer time from terminal to cabin were not observed.
Band issuance, replacement and first-use friction were not tested.
dimensions.reason: The intended arrival sequence is well described, but real handoff performance and recovery remain unobserved.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Inspect port-specific embarkation instructions and test or observe exception handling and credential activation.

dimensions.question: How do digital identity, cabin access, onboard account, service channels and physical ship spaces operate together during the voyage?
dimensions.scopeChange: The stay dimension tests a multi-day mobile institution in which one Sailor identity spans app, Band, cabin and crew-facing systems.

observations.text: The Band is published as the cabin-access and touchless-payment credential for a specific voyage, with an encrypted ID linked to the Sailor's security photo.
Onboard expenses are attached to a personal onboard account, with Band charges linked to the payment method on file and Sailor Services handling billing concerns.
The ship page and app-related guidance indicate that physical spaces and digital service channels are intended to work as one continuous onboard environment.

unanswered: App reliability, connectivity failure, lost-device recovery and cross-system synchronization were not tested.
Actual cabin-service, housekeeping and service-recovery performance remain outside the current evidence.
dimensions.reason: The orchestration model is documented, but its operational reliability has not been observed.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Inspect cabin, housekeeping, Sailor Services and connectivity guidance, then test fallback routes when app or Band access fails.

dimensions.question: How are dining discovery, reservation access, waitlists and dietary needs represented and coordinated?
dimensions.scopeChange: Dining is examined as both a scarce reservable resource and an accessibility/dietary service.

observations.text: Scarlet Lady's public ship page names and describes dining venues, while the dining FAQ publishes reservation windows and channels.
Virgin advises Sailors to recheck for cancellations and permits onboard waitlist handling through restaurants or Sailor Services when reservations are unavailable.
Virgin states that crews ask about allergies and can guide menu choices, while also stating that ships are not allergen-free environments and do not have allergen-free kitchens.

unanswered: Live menu availability, waitlist wait times, dietary-request execution and cross-contamination controls were not tested.
The impact of fare-based reservation timing on dining access remains unmeasured.
dimensions.reason: Booking and dietary guidance are documented, but actual availability and safe execution remain unverified.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Inspect current menus and test reservation, waitlist and dietary escalation paths.

dimensions.question: How are final settlement, disembarkation and unresolved service responsibilities closed at the end of the voyage?
dimensions.scopeChange: Departure includes financial closure and the transition from ship systems back to land-side travel.

observations.text: Virgin states that Band-linked onboard purchases are charged through the onboard account and ultimately to the card on file, with Sailor Services handling billing concerns.
Terminal wheelchair assistance is published for embarkation and disembarkation at home ports.

unanswered: Final folio review, dispute timing, luggage release, disembarkation sequencing and missed onward-travel recovery remain uninspected.
No post-voyage support workflow has yet been added to the evidence set.
dimensions.reason: Some financial and accessibility closure responsibilities are documented, but the full disembarkation journey is not.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Inspect current disembarkation and post-voyage support FAQs, including folio disputes, luggage and onward-travel guidance.

dimensions.question: How does Virgin publicly represent the intended social and sensory atmosphere of Scarlet Lady, and what practical controls are documented?
dimensions.scopeChange: Atmosphere is treated as advertised intent rather than proof of the lived onboard environment.

observations.text: The Scarlet Lady page presents the ship through refreshed social spaces, restaurants, pool areas, nightlife and entertainment, framing the vessel as an active adult leisure environment.
The public narrative emphasizes visual spectacle, nightlife and varied entertainment rather than a single uniform onboard mood.

unanswered: Noise, crowding, sensory load, quiet-space availability and atmosphere across time of day were not observed.
No accessibility-specific sensory environment evidence has yet been inspected.
dimensions.reason: Promotional atmosphere is clear, but practical sensory conditions and guest experience are unverified.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Inspect ship-space policies, quiet-area information and accessibility guidance relevant to sensory conditions.

dimensions.question: Do Scarlet Lady's public images and visual presentation help explain the ship and guest journey as well as promote it?
dimensions.scopeChange: This rating is intentionally narrow because image assets have not yet been directly inspected as a representative sample.

observations.text: The Scarlet Lady page includes a dedicated photo gallery and image-led sections for dining, entertainment and ship spaces.
The same page provides 3D deck-plan orientation alongside promotional imagery, separating some practical navigation from visual marketing.

unanswered: Individual image composition, sequence, responsive crops and mobile presentation have not been directly inspected.
It is not yet established whether practical transitions such as terminal arrival, accessibility, port return or disembarkation are visually explained.
dimensions.reason: A substantial visual layer is present, but the imagery has not yet been audited closely enough to make stronger claims.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Inspect a purposive desktop/mobile image sample and record which stages of the guest journey are visually represented.

dimensions.question: What institutional story and brand narrative does Virgin explicitly attach to Scarlet Lady?
dimensions.scopeChange: Story is limited to attributable public narrative and does not treat brand claims as guest outcomes or cultural legitimacy.

observations.text: Virgin identifies Scarlet Lady as its first ship and gives the Scarlet Lady mermaid a specific symbolic narrative tied to power, leadership and women at the helm.
The ship page connects the vessel's current identity to both its original flagship status and a later refresh of spaces and programming.

unanswered: Independent reception of this narrative and its effect on guest understanding are not established.
The relationship between brand story and actual service behavior remains untested.
dimensions.reason: Virgin's public narrative is directly documented, but independent reception, guest interpretation and operational consistency remain untested.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Keep independent reception and operational consistency as separate hypotheses rather than treating brand story as proof.
